attrs.title: RxnOptBench: Benchmarking LLMs for
attrs.label: RxnOptBench: Benchmarking LLMs for
attrs.research_question: 评估大语言模型在有机方法学中基于真实湿实验数据表进行反应条件优化（选择催化剂、溶剂等以最大化产率和选择性）的能力。
attrs.why_hard: 现有基准仅评估反应分类或逆合成，未要求模型阅读真实条件筛选表并做出比较性决策，且缺乏隔离文献证据与参数记忆的设计。
attrs.abstract: Chemical reaction-condition optimization — choosing the catalyst, ligand, solvent, reagent, temperature, time, and atmosphere that jointly maximize yield and stereoselectivity — is a central, judgement-laden subtask of organic methodology research that large language models are increasingly expected to support. Yet existing chemistry benchmarks evaluate reaction-class labelling, retrosynthesis, or SMILES manipulation, and do not ask models to read a real condition-screening table and pick the best set. We introduce RxnOptBench, a benchmark whose every option and precedent is a real wet-lab entry mined from the optimization tables of organic-methodology papers published in 2025, graded by a continuous relative score derived from a declared headline utility that combines reported yield with enantiomeric excess (ee), diastereomeric ratio (dr), and regioisomeric ratio (rr), and equipped with a paired precedents-vs-no-precedents design that isolates in-context use of literature evidence from parametric memorization. Across nine frontier LLMs and three Chemistry LLMs, even the best models leave substantial headroom: chemistry-specialized models fall to the random-baseline floor on multi-axis selection, while open-weight models have closed most of the gap to proprietary frontier models. We release the final human-reviewed benchmark test set and evaluation code.

attrs.title: ManifoldCache: Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration
attrs.label: ManifoldCache: Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration
attrs.research_question: 如何为受硬几何约束的科学生成扩散模型（CMDMs）设计一种免训练、免数据的推理加速方法，以解决现有加速方法在约束保真度或内存效率上的瓶颈。
attrs.why_hard: 现有加速方法（量化、剪枝、快速求解器、特征缓存）在CMDMs上表现不佳，量化耗尽内存，剪枝破坏约束，快速求解器导致轨迹漂移，特征缓存忽略约束几何。
attrs.abstract: Diffusion models for structured scientific generation must produce samples satisfying hard geometric constraints imposed by physics, chemistry, or biology, yet inference in these settings is prohibitively slow, demanding hundreds to thousands of neural-function evaluations per sample. We unify eight state-of-the-art models spanning medical volumetrics, molecular conformations, protein backbone design, crystal structure prediction, and multi-view 3D scenes under a single abstraction, Constraint-Manifold Diffusion Models (CMDMs), in which the target distribution is supported on a manifold defined by an externally specified constraint map. Existing acceleration families transfer poorly to this class: quantization exhausts memory on high-dimensional volumetric operators; pruning breaks constraint fidelity; fast ODE solvers allow trajectories to drift off the constraint manifold; and feature-caching heuristics are blind to constraint geometry and can cause mode confusion in the high-noise regime. We introduce MANIFOLDCACHE, the first training-free, data-free accelerator designed from first principles for CMDMs. The key insight is that the conditional score decomposes orthogonally into a normal component, which enforces constraint satisfaction, and a tangential component, which navigates within the manifold. Building on this structure, we show for a two-mode Gaussian model that the noise-schedule midpoint, where signal and noise have equal energy, separates two regimes: once signal dominates, the error of a cached estimate is provably bounded, while before that point a strictly positive fraction of cached estimates land in the wrong mode, and this fraction does not vanish as the midpoint is approached. We further prove that, under an explicit condition on the balance between the two score components, deeper network blocks admit larger certified cache strides, as a consequence of the score decomposition propagating through block Jacobians. attrs.title: PharmAgent: Constraint-Aware Search with
attrs.label: PharmAgent: Constraint-Aware Search with
attrs.research_question: 在有限评估预算下，如何利用冻结语言模型结合自适应外部状态（拉格朗日控制器与结构索引回放）进行约束感知的分子优化搜索。
attrs.why_hard: 现有方法需要定制规则或训练来整合化学指令和属性反馈，且缺乏对违规历史的自适应约束控制和结构相关的经验检索。
attrs.abstract: Molecular optimization must improve target activity and satisfy developability constraints within limited evaluation budgets. Classical methods require tailored rules or training to incorporate chemical instructions and property feedback. Frozen language models can condition edits on this information, but need explicit constraint control and relevant experience. We therefore present PHARMAGENT, a constraint-aware molecular search method driven by adaptive external state. Its Lagrangian controller translates violations in accepted states into accumulated constraint pressure, keeping this history separate from current property measurements. Structure-indexed replay complements this feedback with relevant evaluated transitions that guide subsequent proposals. As a curriculum progressively activates constraints, candidates and the incumbent are compared under the same current objective, and the accepted state determines the next multiplier update. We derive an exact identity that characterizes how accepted-state violations accumulate in the controller’s multipliers. Across five tasks with five independent runs, PHARMAGENT achieves a summed area under the target-score curves (AUC) of 3.9208 in target-only search, improving over MOLLEO by 37.3%. With online constraints, it achieves a property-adjusted AUC of 0.7076, improving over the strongest online baseline, ExLLM, by 53.8%. These results rank first among all evaluated methods in both target-only and constraint-aware search. The online comparison covers all five baseline frameworks. The full system leads every ablation variant in target quality, property-adjusted performance, and Pareto hypervolume. All five molecular cases reach feasible final states, documenting target gains and trade-offs. These results establish PHARMAGENT as a powerful framework for budget-limited molecular optimization, achieving leading aggregate performance through adaptive external search state and frozen language models.

attrs.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulations proceed by integrating the Langevin equations over many small femtosecond timesteps. This poses a challenge for estimating ensemble properties and transition dynamics that occur on much longer timescales. We introduce Langevin Flow Maps, which extend machine-learned force-fields to additionally learn the stochastic Langevin integrator. We show that Langevin Flow Maps enable large-timestep molecular dynamics and recover accurate dynamical properties of the system, while running an order of magnitude faster than current machine-learned force fields. Further, by training on a diverse molecular dataset, we demonstrate a path towards transferable Langevin Flow Maps.

attrs.research_question: 如何通过结合科学文献证据与序列生成模型，解决多目标抗菌肽设计中的证据到执行差距，实现可靠的序列干预。

attrs.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can reason over scientific literature and formulate complex design strategies, yet they struggle to translate these strategies into reliable biological sequence manipulations. Protein language models and related generators capture complex sequence patterns but are not inherently equipped to integrate literature evidence into multi-step reasoning and reflective decision-making. This separation creates an evidence-to-execution gap between scientific reasoning and sequence-level control. We introduce EASER (Evidence-Aware Sequence Engineering with Reflection), a reflective agent that connects scientific reasoning with sequence generation through a learned property interface. The interface consists of property-specific low-rank matrices trained offline and kept fixed during search. The agent combines these matrices to steer a specialized diffusion generator. Using retrieved biological evidence, sequence context, and prior outcomes, it proposes intervention hypotheses specifying anchors, editable positions, and control coefficients. Probe-and-Steer tests these interventions and uses predicted property responses to allocate further samples. The agent reflects on the outcomes to guide subsequent decisions. We evaluate EASER on computational antimicrobial peptide design, balancing activity, non-hemolysis, and non-toxicity. At matched decision states, explicit hypothesis formulation yields larger multi-objective gains than direct action generation. Ablations support the contributions of evidence retrieval, episodic history, reflection, and Probe-and-Steer. Across six independent runs, EASER achieves the highest mean hypervolume and lowest mean IGD+ among the evaluated search policies and generators on screened candidates. The AMP experiments illustrate how an executable property interface and iterative feedback connect scientific reasoning with specialized sequence generation.

attrs.research_question: How can verified scientific executions drive persistent and transferable program-level self-evolution without updating foundation-model parameters?
attrs.why_hard: repairs rarely persist
attrs.abstract: Large language model agents are accelerating scientific automation, yet verified executions rarely become persistent programlevel improvements, and existing evaluations do not examine this process across sequential tasks in both the natural and social sciences. We formalize ScienceClaw as fixed-parameter program self-evolution that unifies task solving, scientific verification, and program updates. ScienceClaw-Eval spans 23 disciplines and measures scientific correctness, evolutionary gain, retention, crossdataset transfer, and evolution cost through sequential streams and independent reset evaluation. Our framework repairs executable workflows through multi-turn interaction, converts re-executionverified failure–success trajectories into linked Skill and Operator candidates, and retains an update only when source-task replay reproduces the repair and independent scientific tasks improve. Code is available at https://github.com/beita6969/ScienceClaw.

attrs.title: MD-LLM-2: A Transferable Language Model of Molecular Dynamics with Physical Conditioning and Explicit Path Probabilities
attrs.label: MD-LLM-2: A Transferable Language Model of Molecular Dynamics with Physical Conditioning and Explicit Path Probabilities
attrs.research_question: 开发一个可迁移的语言模型，基于序列、温度和历史条件生成分子动力学轨迹，并显式建模路径概率。
attrs.why_hard: 跨越自由能垒和采样多个热力学条件在计算上代价高昂，且现有方法通常针对特定蛋白或需要预定义集体变量。
attrs.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations model the motion of proteins between conformational states, but crossing free energy barriers and sampling multiple thermodynamic conditions remain computationally costly. We recently introduced MD-LLM-1, which showed that language models can generate conformational trajectories at lower cost, but required a separate model for each protein and did not explicitly model thermodynamics or kinetics. Here we introduce MD-LLM-2, a transferable language model that generates trajectories conditioned on sequence, temperature and molecular history. Because each step defines a normalized distribution over structural tokens, the model assigns an explicit likelihood to every generated or simulated trajectory. Trained across mdCATH domains, MD-LLM-2 reproduces the median radius of gyration of MD within 1 Å in 10 of 12 unseen domains, predicts reduced Trp-cage compaction at higher temperature, and generates L99A T4 lysozyme trajectories that reach published transition-region backbone structures. In alanine dipeptide simulations, conditioning on a torsional scaling parameter λ predicts basin populations at unseen couplings with a mean absolute error of 0.09 versus 0.35 for MBAR, and first-passage probabilities with an error of 0.08 versus 0.16 for a reversible Markov state model. Frame-isoentropic sampling further limits the accumulation of errors during autoregressive trajectory generation. Together, these results extend MD-LLM from protein-specific trajectory generation to transferable, physically conditioned modelling with explicit path likelihoods, and show that the framework can predict equilibrium populations for force-field parameters not seen during training, with an initial indication that first-passage kinetics can also be captured.

attrs.abstract: Unified atomistic modeling has the potential to accelerate discovery in chemistry, materials science, and biology by bridging data-rich chemical domains and data-scarce biological contexts. However, existing generative approaches to atomistic modeling remain highly specialized to scientific disciplines (chemistry vs. biology) or do not leverage both high-volume organic (molecule) and inorganic (material) data for general-purpose pretraining. To this end, we introduce Zatom-2, an atomistic generative model pretrained on approximately five million structures from the OMol25 and OMat24 electronic structure datasets. Zatom-2 features a multiscale Transformer architecture coupled with conditional flow matching that supports force conditioning and foundational pretraining tasks such as generation, structure prediction, and prediction of molecular and material energies and forces. Empirically, Zatom-2 achieves better molecular distribution fidelity than Zatom-1 and achieves strong performance on existing molecule and material generation benchmarks. Zatom-2 demonstrates the ability to control sample generation across low- and high-force regimes, and enhances protein generation in a low-data setting through joint generative-predictive pretraining and transfer learning, increasing protein backbone designability in a length extrapolation setting from 67.8% without pretraining to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.

nodes.label: ELUCIDATING THE SPACE OF ENZYMATIC REACTION:

attrs.title: ELUCIDATING THE SPACE OF ENZYMATIC REACTION:
attrs.label: ELUCIDATING THE SPACE OF ENZYMATIC REACTION:
attrs.research_question: 构建统一基准 VenusRX-Bench 和预训练模型 VenusRX，以学习连接反应物、产物和酶委(EC)注释的酶促反应空间。
attrs.why_hard: 现有有机反应模型未设计用于纳入酶特征，且酶促反应数据稀缺、分散且缺乏标准化基准，导致难以捕捉酶促转化的复杂性。
attrs.abstract: Existing reaction models primarily learn molecular transformations, whereas enzymatic reactions depend jointly on molecular structure and catalytic function. We formulate this problem as learning an enzymatic reaction space linking reactants, products, and Enzyme Commission (EC) annotations. To characterize this space, we introduce VenusRX-Bench, a unified benchmark for forward reaction prediction, single-step retrosynthesis, and EC-number prediction. VenusRX-Bench integrates reactions from multiple biochemical databases with standardized curation, leakage-controlled splits, and consistent evaluation. Benchmarking representative chemical and enzymatic models reveals a clear chemical-to-enzymatic domain gap, driven by limited domain data, catalytic-context dependency, and the difficulty of modeling large biomolecular structures. To bridge this gap, we develop VenusRX, a unified T5-style sequence-to-sequence model for enzymatic reactions. VenusRX jointly learns forward prediction, retrosynthesis, and reaction reconstruction, with two-stage training on millions of template-expanded reactions followed by real biochemical reactions. In addition, optional EC conditioning incorporates catalytic context, while Molecule Library-Constrained Decoding improves the generation of complex biomolecules. Across benchmark tasks and challenging generalization splits, VenusRX achieves the best or competitive performance on most evaluated settings over representative chemical and enzymatic baselines. Moreover, EC information consistently improves reaction prediction, while learned reaction representations support accurate EC prediction, revealing a bidirectional relationship between reaction structure and catalytic function. Together, VenusRX-Bench and VenusRX provide a unified framework for elucidating and modeling enzymatic reaction space.

attrs.research_question: 研究LLM在神经算子微调中是依赖初始任务上下文还是根据实验反馈调整决策，通过受控干预验证其决策机制。

attrs.abstract: Do LLM scientific agents rely only on their initial task context, or do they adapt their decisions in response to experimental feedback? We study this question in neural operator adaptation, where a large language model (LLM) selects fine-tuning configurations under a limited trial budget. Across transfers within and between partial differential equation (PDE) families, the LLM achieves lower held-out test nRMSE than random search and Bayesian optimisation in nearly every matched comparison. Endpoint performance alone cannot distinguish what happens, so we verify each attribution with controlled interventions. Before observing any validation score, the LLM’s first configuration already ranks near the top of the corresponding random-search pool, indicating a useful initial bias. A complementary cold-start intervention shows that the selected base learning rate shifts with the PDE description. Once feedback becomes available, reassigning validation scores among evaluated configurations changes the next proposal in every case tested, whereas a value-preserving rewrite produces no comparable aggregate effect. These interventions establish that the LLM’s decision-level actions respond to the given task and observed outcomes, showing that it combines a task-dependent prior with sensitivity to experimental feedback.

attrs.research_question: 研究如何通过联合离散序列与SE(3)结构扩散，为任意靶点设计具有几何与理化互补性的高亲和力蛋白结合剂。

attrs.abstract: The design of high-affinity, target-specific protein binders is central to the development of modern therapeutics. However, existing proteingeneration methods remain limited in this setting, as many generated designs fail to simultaneously achieve geometric and physicochemical complementarity at binding interfaces. To address this challenge, we introduce PIDiff, a physicochemically enhanced multimodal diffusion framework for protein–protein complex design. PIDiff jointly designs target-conditioned protein sequences and structures by coupling diffusion in discrete sequence space with diffusion on the continuous $S E ( 3 )$ structural manifold. At its core, PIDiff employs PIFormer, a novel architecture that interleaves geometry-aware invariant point attention with global sequence self-attention. We further curate PIBench, a protein–protein complex dataset with diverse target scaffolds derived from the Protein Data Bank (PDB). We first pretrain PIDiff on PIBench and subsequently fine-tune it for two therapeutically relevant applications: minibinder design and antibody design. PPFrame consistently outperforms baseline methods across sequence design success rate, structure binding energy, and sequence-structure co-designability on all tasks.

attrs.research_question: 如何利用前向反应一致性反馈优化单步逆合成反应物生成，以解决参考集训练无法覆盖未记录可行反应物的问题

attrs.abstract: Single-step retrosynthesis is inherently a one-tomany inverse problem, yet most models are trained and evaluated against a single recorded reactant set. Reference-based training provides no explicit positive signal for unrecorded alternatives, while exact-match evaluation counts non-matching predictions as incorrect regardless of their chemical plausibility. We propose Retrosynthesis via Reinforcement Learning from Forward Feedback (RetroRLFF), which optimizes reactant generation using forward consistency with the target product rather than reference agreement alone. Starting from a supervised decoderonly Transformer, RetroRLFF generates complete reactant candidates and uses a frozen forward reaction model to predict products for comparison with the target. A sequence-level reward retains reference agreement to preserve recovery of recorded reactions and adds forward consistency to provide feedback for non-reference candidates, while penalizing invalid outputs. Direct Advantage-Based Policy Optimization then updates the retrosynthesis policy from this feedback without requiring human preference annotations or a preference-trained reward model. On USPTO-50K, RetroRLFF outperforms all 14 baselines in candidate-level round-trip accuracy at $k \in \{ 1 , 3 , 5 , 1 0 \}$ . With approximately 50 million parameters, it reaches $9 0 . 1 \%$ top-1 round-trip accuracy, exceeding R-SMILES, the strongest competing baseline on this metric, by 8.5 percentage points. Relative to its supervised policy, round-trip accuracy improves from $8 3 . 1 \%$ to $9 0 . 1 \%$ , while exact-match accuracy is maintained at $5 7 . 9 \%$ versus $5 7 . 5 \%$ . To complement forward-model-based evaluation, we conduct an anonymized expert assessment on 131 randomly selected test cases, in which organic synthesis experts prefer RetroRLFF over EditRetro in $67 . 9 \%$ of comparisons. attrs.research_question: 如何在LLM逆合成规划中通过多路线联合扩展和多目标推理，在有限搜索预算下优化反应合理性、往返一致性和起始物料价格。

attrs.abstract: Multi-step retrosynthesis planning is often considered solved once a route to purchasable starting materials is found, but such a route should also be practical in real-world chemistry. Recent LLM-based planners formulate this process as sequential decision-making over an AND-OR graph, yet typically expand a single molecule per turn and are optimized for solvability alone, leaving alternative routes uncompared across the multiple objectives that determine practicality before the search budget is committed. We introduce RETROPLANNER, an LLM-based planner that jointly compares multiple routes to steer the search toward higher synthesizability, as measured by reaction plausibility, round-trip consistency, and starting-material price. RETROPLANNER is trained to reason over chemical evidence: structural progress from the target molecule, bond changes and reaction classes, where candidate routes diverge from one another, and how they rank across multiple objectives. Experiments on multi-step retrosynthesis benchmarks demonstrate that RETROPLANNER recovers more alternative routes than prior LLM-based planners while improving synthetic route quality and maintaining a high success rate.

attrs.research_question: 如何构建一种拓扑感知的分子语言，使片段级表示学习能与精确的结构编辑相结合，同时保持化学单元的显式地址性。

attrs.abstract: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing, optimization, transformation transfer and change identification by 9 to 56 percentage points over plain SMILES. Together, these results establish an executable molecular language in which learned chemical units remain directly operable during design.

attrs.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
attrs.label: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
attrs.research_question: 研究如何利用强化学习训练LLM，通过多轮反馈向量（属性改进与相似度）迭代优化分子，以在保持结构相似性的同时提升多个分子属性。
attrs.why_hard: 现有LLM方法未在训练阶段显式利用多轮反馈，仅依赖推理时提示或单轮生成，缺乏对迭代反馈机制的专门训练。
attrs.abstract: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over GeLLM3O, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate GeLLM3O-MFG on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that GeLLM3O-MFG achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate (81.50%), outperforming the base model GeLLM3O (70.81%).

attrs.research_question: 评估LLM在隐藏目标实体身份、仅通过源实体和结构编辑定义目标时的化学预测能力，以区分真实推理与记忆检索。
attrs.why_hard: 现有评估直接提供目标身份信息，难以区分模型预测源于可迁移的结构-性质推理还是依赖上下文线索或记忆检索。
attrs.abstract: Large language models have achieved strong performance on chemical prediction benchmarks. However, existing evaluation methods typically provide the identity information of the target entity directly, making it difficult to determine whether model predictions arise from transferable structure–property reasoning capabilities or rely on target-related contextual information or memory retrieval. We propose the Identity-Blinded Reasoning Diagnostic framework to evaluate chemical prediction models when target entity identity information is hidden. In this framework, the target is no longer directly defined by its entity identity, but instead by a known source entity and an explicit structural edit operation. This setting preserves the information required to determine the target while reducing the opportunity for models to access target identity cues. We evaluate this framework across six tasks spanning odor prediction, molecular property prediction, retrosynthesis, and reaction yield prediction. The results show that models generally achieve better prediction performance when the properties of the source entity and target entity are consistent. Providing explicit source entity labels further strengthens this dependence. Moreover, while keeping the target entity, structural change, and ground-truth label unchanged, replacing only the source entity label causes some model predictions to systematically shift toward the substituted source labels.These results indicate that high benchmark accuracy in chemical prediction tasks does not necessarily imply that large language models possess reliable structure–property reasoning capabilities. Our diagnostic framework provides a controlled evaluation approach for testing whether models can genuinely update predictions according to entity changes. The framework can be extended to other AI for Science tasks, particularly those where targets can be defined through transformations of known entities.

attrs.title: MolHop: Scaffold-Hopping Molecular Design with Agentic
attrs.label: MolHop: Scaffold-Hopping Molecular Design with Agentic
attrs.research_question: 提出MolHop框架，通过层级化骨架导航与代理强化学习，在保持参考分子功能特性的同时发现具有完全不同骨架的替代分子。
attrs.why_hard: 现有LLM代理通常仅在现有结构邻域内进行局部优化，缺乏探索广阔化学空间以发现不同骨架分子的能力。
attrs.abstract: Molecular design is often formulated as an optimization problem over existing molecular spaces. However, molecular optimization and the discovery of structurally distinct replacement molecules represent two fundamentally different search problems. LLM-based molecular design agents typically perform the former, conducting local refinement within the neighborhood of existing structures to improve target properties through structural modifications. In contrast, the latter requires exploration of a broader chemical space to discover molecules with entirely different scaffolds while preserving the functional characteristics of reference molecules. We propose MolHop, an agentic framework for cross-scaffold molecular discovery that enables models to navigate and edit within a pre-organized chemical space. MolHop organizes approximately 1.6 million molecular scaffolds from commercial molecules into a coarse-to-fine hierarchical action space. The agent selects new exploration regions through scaffold navigation actions and adjusts candidate properties through molecular editing. The framework maintains historical trajectory memory to support long-horizon search processes. On drug molecule and commercial compound tasks, connecting Grok-4.6 and DeepSeek-Flash-V4.1 to the MolHop framework substantially improves their cross-scaffold joint success rates. We develop MolHop-9B through agentic reinforcement learning, and MolHop-9B outperforms generative baselines including GPT-5.6-sol, Claude-5-Opus, and Gemini-3.1-Pro, while generating candidate molecules with larger scaffold differences from the reference molecules. These results demonstrate that effective molecular discovery beyond the traditional optimization paradigm requires structured chemical and action spaces, enabling agents to explore new structural regions rather than merely refine existing molecules.

attrs.title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in
attrs.label: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in
attrs.research_question: 如何训练LLM审计员通过多轮工具交互探测代理在有效任务执行中的策略违规
attrs.why_hard: 策略违规效果可能在多轮后出现，跨越多个工具调用或在下游系统显现，难以审计
attrs.abstract: Modern agentic systems extend language models with external tools, enabling them to complete complex tasks through multi-turn interactions. As these agents are deployed in consequential settings, their behavior is often constrained by policies governing pricing, privacy, confirmation, safety, and other operational requirements. However, existing evaluation methods leave a critical gap: capability benchmarks measure what agents can accomplish, while content-safety red-teaming measures harmful generations, but neither tests whether agents comply with predefined policies during otherwise valid tool use. Such policy violations are difficult to audit because their effects may emerge only after several turns, span multiple tool calls, or surface in downstream systems. We propose PROBE1 (Policy Rule Observation via Behavioral Exploration), an algorithm for training LLM-based auditors that interact with deployed target agents as realistic users and probe them for policy violations through multi-turn, tool-mediated dialogue. We formalize agent auditing as a two-player Markov game and propose a composite reward that balances violation discovery, behavioral plausibility, conversation progress, and policy diversity. To study the role of training objectives and reward design, we compare GRPO, DPO, and GFlowNet-based optimization in a controlled setting. Across extensive experiments, auditors trained with PROBE uncover substantially broader and higher-yield policy violations than same-architecture zero-shot adversaries, even when the auditor is significantly smaller than the target agent. Our results show that multi-turn behavioral auditing is a distinct and necessary axis of agent evaluation, complementing capability and content-safety benchmarks. PROBE offers a scalable path toward automated policy auditing for real-world agentic systems and suggests a future co-evolutionary loop in which auditors expose failures and agents improve from auditor feedback.

attrs.title: REVISITING STRUCTURE-BASED FILTERING FOR AI-
attrs.label: REVISITING STRUCTURE-BASED FILTERING FOR AI-
attrs.research_question: 研究结构预测输出（如AlphaFold 3）能否有效筛选AI设计的抗体，以平衡假阳性与假阴性，优先实验验证。
attrs.why_hard: 现有序列级筛选缺乏靶点特异性证据，而结构预测置信度在区分不同抗原与同一抗原内候选时表现不一致。
attrs.abstract: AI antibody design can generate far more candidates than can be experimentally tested, making post-generation filtering a central bottleneck. We study whether structure-prediction outputs can help prioritize AI-designed antibodies for experimental validation. We evaluate this problem on 4,184 experimentally characterized antibody–antigen pairs, combining newly generated wet-lab measurements with curated affinity data across diverse antigens and assay settings. We introduce two complementary filtering signals: Regional Interaction Contrast (RIC), which captures support for the predicted antibody–antigen interface, and Non-CDR Antibody Confidence (NAC), which measures antibody confidence outside the CDRs. Across AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, and OpenDDE, we find a striking difference in what information matters for filtering. Interface evidence is strongest when comparing candidates designed for different antigens, whereas antibody-level reliability is substantially more informative for ranking candidates within the same antigen. In particular, non-CDR antibody confidence improves the average within-antigen filtering rank over whole-antibody confidence across predictors, revealing an unexpected source of filtering signal beyond the predicted interface. Finally, we examine the information encoded in the predictor outputs themselves. Predicted structures contain substantial but incomplete binding-related signal, revealing both the opportunities and limits of structure-based filtering: better metrics can exploit current predictors more effectively, but their performance ultimately remains constrained by what those predictors can distinguish. Code is available in the code repository.

attrs.title: ReTRACE: Feedback-Guided LLM Agent in a
attrs.label: ReTRACE: Feedback-Guided LLM Agent in a
attrs.research_question: 如何利用LLM代理在化学工具框架中协调单步预测引擎与多准则评估器，以解决复杂目标分子的全局逆合成路线规划问题
attrs.why_hard: 现有搜索算法将化学判断压缩为标量分数，难以应用全路线约束或解释分支选择原因
attrs.abstract: Computer-aided retrosynthesis has advanced through single-step prediction, tree search and route scoring, but complex targets still require judgement over the whole route, where stereochemistry, functional-group compatibility, cost and greenness interact. Here we present ReTRACE (REtrosynthesis with Tool-orchestrated Reasoning And Context-aware Evidence), an agent that places a large language model (LLM) in a chemistry harness that integrates molecular tools, complementary single-step prediction engines, a purchasable starting-material library, a route memory and a multi-criterion route evaluator. Routes are judged by a new metric that combines programmatic checks with adversarial LLM review, and its verdicts are compared with a synthetic chemist’s. The agent learns continually from evaluator feedback during search, diagnosing weak routes and backtracking to revise them. With Claude Opus 4.8, at least one of the top 10 routes proposed by ReTRACE passed the audit for 87.4%, 95.0% and 86.7% of targets on the three benchmarks. Two prospective wet-lab syntheses show that ReTRACE route proposals can be converted into executable procedures after expert revision.

nodes.label: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?

attrs.title: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?
attrs.label: Do AI-for-Science Agents Preserve Model Safety?
attrs.research_question: 评估当LLM集成到AI-for-Science智能体框架中时，模型安全性是否得以保留，特别是在有害化学请求下的表现。
attrs.why_hard: 现有方法通常仅评估基础模型，未考虑智能体框架引入的新交互路径对安全性的影响。
attrs.abstract: AI-for-Science agents are increasingly being used for formulating scientific hypotheses, running autonomous experiments, and interpreting evidence. These agents are constructed by integrating a large language model (LLM) into a domain-specific agent harness, which in turn can improve the LLM’s scientific capability and enable the model to orchestrate scientific tools. In this work, we ask whether model safety is preserved when an LLM is integrated in an AI-for-Science agent harness. We evaluate five agent harnesses on 50 harmful chemistry requests. Specifically, we study how the safety behavior changes under direct prompting, two simple adversarial prompting strategies, and an adaptive attack. Across four recent GPT variants, our results show that the agent harness can increase harmful compliance even under direct prompting. More critically, we find that adaptive attacks that are largely unsuccessful against the base LLM suddenly become highly successful after the agent harness is introduced. Our results show that the safety behavior of the base LLM is not durable once a harness is introduced. Thus, as AI-for-Science agents become more capable and autonomous, the community needs to evaluate and align the agent using domain-specific safety benchmarks.

attrs.title: REMEDI: INFERENCE-TIME REFINEMENT AND SELF-
attrs.label: REMEDI: INFERENCE-TIME REFINEMENT AND SELF-
attrs.research_question: 如何利用预训练分子语言模型在推理时通过Metropolis-Hastings搜索进行可控的多目标分子优化，并蒸馏以提升零样本生成能力
attrs.why_hard: 基于RL的后训练依赖昂贵的任务特定数据集，且难以实现多目标优化和跨任务迁移
attrs.abstract: In drug development, lead optimization must improve competing properties, such as increasing permeability and reducing toxicity, while limiting scaffold changes that could compromise the lead’s potency. RL-based post-training, such as C-MORAL, addresses this problem by fine-tuning molecular language models to directly optimize molecular leads for objectives of interest, which relies on expensive task-specific datasets and faces challenges in achieving multi-objective optimization (MOO). We argue a pretrained model may already contain useful molecular edits that zero-shot generation cannot efficiently reach. Motivated by the limited search capabilities of zero-shot generation, we develop an efficient Metropolis–Hastings search strategy to better explore the proposal distribution. We propose ReMedI, which uses the molecular language model as a base proposer for inference-time alignment. Given a lead and a set of multi-objective tasks, the model proposes edits conditioned on the current molecule, while Metropolis–Hastings refinement guides sequential edits under an objective for property improvement, preservation, and lead similarity. On both C-MuMOInstruct and SMDD benchmarks, refinement improves frozen base models across three backbones, reaching significantly higher multi-objective optimization success rates compared to baselines. These search traces can then distilled into the base model which improves zero-shot generation and subsequent search using ≈7.8× less training molecular leads than that of C-MORAL. ReMedI achieves ≈2.8× the strict-success coverage of RL baseline C-MORAL, including on out-of-distribution tasks, with matched lead-relative similarity.

attrs.title: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets?
attrs.label: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets?
attrs.research_question: 研究在基于结构的药物设计中，LLM智能体优化配体时，从已知蛋白口袋获得的编辑经验能否通过特定键值迁移到未见过的口袋。
attrs.why_hard: 现有方法（如PROBE）产生的编辑响应仅用于当前实例，未形成可跨实例复用的经验库，且缺乏能同时利用口袋与配体信息并在新口袋上有效区分编辑效果的键值。
attrs.abstract: LLM agents optimize a ligand in a protein pocket by editing it step by step and docking each edit. Recent agents first spend extra dockings probing the complex with controlled edits; guidance induced from these probes is reported to help more than the chemical knowledge the model already carries. The probes are then discarded with the instance that produced them, so the obvious next step is to keep them in an experience base, letting a new pocket inherit what earlier ones already paid for. Such a base is read through a key: the record properties under which past edits are pooled and a new one is looked up. Using the full log of one such run over the CrossDocked2020 test-set pockets, we ask whether its keys recur on a pocket the base has never seen and still separate improving from worsening edits. Using the contacts at the site being edited, the action, and the round as a key, the base separates them sharply. Within our analysis, this separation is largely explained by how much the edit changed the molecule’s size, the action, and the round, none of which describes the target. That is not because the target is irrelevant: naming it outright separates them several times more sharply. For a pocket absent from the base, transfer must rely on a description rather than its identity. Among the exact-match descriptions we evaluate, the more specific ones rarely recur, whereas the coarser ones provide little separation; the signals that do transfer primarily describe the edit and the molecule it produced rather than the target. Under the representations and lookup scheme studied here, an experience base may be more useful for prioritizing an agent’s own proposals for docking than for directly prescribing what to build.

attrs.label: Agent-guided epitope excision enables
attrs.research_question: 如何通过截断靶点至局部界面窗口（epitope excision）并结合智能体优化，加速de novo结合蛋白设计并提高命中率
attrs.why_hard: 全靶点结构预测和扩散生成计算耗时过长，且大靶点中远离结合位点的区域占用大量计算资源
attrs.abstract: De novo protein design campaigns remain bottlenecked by the inference compute time required to generate and rank candidates, limiting wider functional exploration. Here, we introduce and evaluate an epitope excision approach that truncates targets to local interface windows to accelerate both backbone diffusion and structure prediction. Across 15 targets and 3,666 designs, excised windows closely reproduced full-target binding interfaces (median C𝛼RMSD of 0.37 Å) and made it practical to design binders against the 719-residue extracellular domain of fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAP) by cutting RFdiffusion and AlphaFold3 GPU time by ∼88% in one of the epitopes. Pairing this workflow with an agentic optimization loop allowed the system to autonomously identify catalytic-site targeting strategies. Under a fixed compute budget, a human-in-the-loop (HITL) workflow raised the computational hit rate from 5.06% to 9.33% while further cutting GPU hours by ∼42%. We also found that omitting target multiple sequence alignments during refolding roughly substantially increased the apparent yield. Wet-lab validation with yeast display identified nanomolar binders from the generated designs with the HITL and the fully autonomous agent (human-out-of-the-loop, HOOTL) arms recovering more enriched designs than the PI-alone baseline. Together, target excision and agent-guided search offer a practical way to scale de novo binder design to large, therapeutically relevant proteins.

attrs.title: MLIPDiff: Guiding Denoising Diffusion Models for
attrs.label: MLIPDiff: Guiding Denoising Diffusion Models for
attrs.research_question: 如何利用机器学习原子间势（MLIP）在推理阶段引导预训练扩散模型，以生成物理上合理且无碰撞的配体结构。
attrs.why_hard: 现有扩散模型仅拟合参考结构分布，常产生与蛋白碰撞或局部几何畸变的物理不合理构象。
attrs.abstract: Diffusion models have become a dominant approach to structure-based drug design. However, because they are trained primarily to fit reference structures, they often place ligands in physically implausible poses that clash with the protein. We introduce MLIPDiff, an inference-time guidance method that can be applied to pre-trained diffusion models for ligand generation. The method uses physics-informed guidance from UMA (Universal Models for Atoms), a machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP). The guidance combines four weighted energy terms (protein-ligand interaction, ligand strain, steric clash, and pocket anchoring) and uses the original model checkpoint without retraining. On CrossDocked2020, MLIPDiff completely eliminates protein-ligand collisions while preserving the ligand’s local geometry, improving bond-length distributions and physical plausibility relative to the base model. Compared to models such as NucleusDiff that are specifically designed to reduce atomic clashes, MLIPDiff achieves clash-free structures without compromising local geometry. It maintains the base model’s PoseBusters pass rate and attains the best median Vina Score, Vina Min, and Vina Dock, surpassing both the base model and NucleusDiff, with a median of 59.6% of ligands per pocket binding more strongly than the reference. MLIPDiff thus addresses a limitation of prior methods by generating physically plausible structures with favorable predicted binding affinity using a single frozen model and no additional training.

attrs.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) carry out their functions through heterogeneous conformational ensembles that reflect their dynamics, yet most protein function prediction methods rely on sequence or a single static structure. To this end, we introduce DynaReason-Pro, the first framework to jointly predict GO terms from conformational ensembles and generate natural-language functional rationales. We evaluate DynaReason-Pro on a curated IDP benchmark from the Protein Ensemble Database (PED), with sequence- and structure-cluster-disjoint splits to prevent data leakage. Variability-stratified evaluation shows the clearest gains in the high-conformational-variability regime.

attrs.abstract: AI has made significant contributions to scientific discovery. Autonomous agents can now independently analyse complex problems, design experiments, write and execute code, analyse findings, and derive scientific conclusions. Nevertheless, errors in AI-generated code, experimental procedures, or evidence interpretation can lead to invalid research conclusions, undermining the reliability and reproducibility of automated scientific discovery. In this vision paper, we propose Software Engineering for AI-Driven Science (SE4AI4Sci) as an emerging research area for addressing this challenge. As an organising framework, we introduce the Scientific Assurance Chain, connecting intent, experimental design, implementation, execution, evidence, and claim. Through six documented failures in recent AI-for-science systems, we show where this chain can break, where existing assurance mechanisms fall short, and what new research challenges follow. We also outline a research agenda for adapting and extending software engineering techniques across the chain.

attrs.title: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
attrs.label: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
attrs.research_question: 开发一种保留所有重原子并隐式处理溶剂的粗粒度神经网络势，以在可访问时间尺度内模拟生物分子复合物（包括蛋白-配体）的动力学。
attrs.why_hard: 全原子分子动力学难以在可访问时间尺度内捕捉生物分子复合物中涉及的稀有事件。
attrs.abstract: The behavior of biomolecular complexes is governed by chemically specific interactions and often involves rare events that atomistic molecular dynamics struggle to capture within accessible timescales. Here we introduce AMARO v2.0, a coarse-grained neural network potential that retains all heavy atoms and treats solvent implicitly. Hydrogen-aware bead types and total-charge conditioning provide a shared representation for proteins, drug-like molecules, and their complexes, including ternary protein–protein–ligand systems. The model preserves folded proteins and captures key features of protein conformational free-energy landscapes. Across 262 complexes spanning 11 targets, the learned potential retains most ligand poses, although quaternary structure reorientation is observed for the HIF2A ternary complex. In targeted case studies, AMARO v2.0 distinguishes the two protonation states of trypsin–benzamidine and reaches the crystal binding pose in 3.3-fold more trajectories than all-atom molecular mechanics at a fixed estimated GPU-time budget. The same framework also recovers a reference binding pose in TYK2 and supports binding free-energy estimation for both trypsin–benzamidine and TYK2–EJM31, although the resulting values are more energetically favorable than the experimental references. SHP2 and CDK8 systems expose remaining limitations in binding-pose recovery and site specificity, respectively. Together, these results support AMARO v2.0 as a shared heavy-atom potential for biomolecular complex dynamics.

attrs.research_question: 评估AI智能体能否跨学科复现科学论文中的实验，将不完整描述转化为可执行工作流并生成可验证证据。
attrs.why_hard: 现有基准多聚焦AI/ML，跨学科复现需操作领域专用软件、处理物理数值选择及诊断长时计算，且需区分有效证据与看似合理的输出。
attrs.abstract: Before AI can be trusted to discover new science, it should be able to reproduce what science already knows. Reproduction provides a rigorous checkpoint for an AI scientist: the target claim is known, yet recovering it still requires translating an incomplete scientific description into an executable experiment and producing evidence that can be independently verified. Existing research-reproduction benchmarks largely focus on AI and machine learning, where experiments share relatively homogeneous software stacks. Extending this capability across scientific disciplines introduces a different challenge: agents must operate domain-specific scientific software, make physical and numerical choices, diagnose long-running computations, and distinguish valid evidence from merely plausible outputs. We introduce PAPERBENCHX, a benchmark of 93 expert-constructed paper-reproduction tasks spanning 12 research areas across electromagnetics, photonics, chemistry, materials science, biology, and robotics. Each task provides the source paper, a public task specification, and a domain-native scientific environment involving specialized scientific software. Agents must reconstruct a key experiment, execute and diagnose it, and deliver a runnable workflow that supports the target scientific claim. To evaluate scientific validity rather than surface-level agreement, we replay every submission from scratch and score only regenerated evidence against expert-validated criteria. Across 10 frontier agent configurations, the best configuration fully reproduces only 14% tasks under the 90% threshold. Meanwhile, mean rubric scores range from 27.53% to 59.08%, indicating that substantial partial progress rarely translates into complete scientific reproduction. These results reveal a large gap between paper understanding and reliably producing reproducible scientific evidence.

attrs.title: TACFORMER: TRANSFORMER-BASED GENERATIVE MODEL
attrs.label: TACFORMER: TRANSFORMER-BASED GENERATIVE MODEL
attrs.research_question: 提出TACFormer，利用ESM-2预训练的POI序列表征作为条件，生成完整的de novo PROTAC分子，而非仅生成linker。
attrs.why_hard: 现有方法多将PROTAC设计简化为linker生成，固定warhead和E3配体，限制了化学空间探索且未显式利用蛋白水平信息。
attrs.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) represents a fundamental shift in drug discovery, moving beyond traditional target inhibition toward the event-driven removal of disease-causing proteins. A prominent strategy for TPD is the use of proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs), heterobifunctional molecules that selectively route a protein of interest (POI) to the ubiquitin–proteasome system for degradation. While PROTAC design still relies heavily on trial-and-error synthesis and experimental testing, deep generative models offer a promising means to explore PROTAC chemical space in silico and generate novel molecules. However, many existing generative methods formulate PROTAC design primarily as a linker-generation problem, with POI-binding (warhead) and E3-ligase-binding components fixed in advance. This restricts exploration of the full PROTAC chemical space and often leaves the POI implicit through the predefined warhead, rather than using protein-level information as an explicit conditioning signal during generation. To address these limitations, we propose TACFormer: a transformer-based generative model for target-aware de novo PROTAC design. The model conditions a GPT-style molecular decoder on pretrained ESM-2 representations of POI sequences, allowing POI-level information to steer full-molecule generation. Our results show that TACFormer generates highly novel and chemically diverse PROTACs while showing consistent POI-dependent shifts in generated chemical space. In particular, molecules generated under specific target conditions preferentially populate chemical neighborhoods associated with POIs in the held-out dataset, while extrapolating to novel chemotypes. By natively integrating biological context into the generative process, TACFormer moves PROTAC design toward a more biology-informed exploration of degrader chemical space.

attrs.title: TRANSFERRING PEPTIDE–TARGET INTERACTION PAT-
attrs.label: TRANSFERRING PEPTIDE–TARGET INTERACTION PAT-
attrs.research_question: 如何通过联合引导离散扩散和流匹配，将肽-靶标相互作用模式迁移到小分子生成中，以解决PPI界面约束不足的问题

attrs.abstract: Generating small molecules to target protein-protein interactions (PPIs) remains one of the most challenging yet high-reward frontiers in drug discovery. Unlike traditional small-molecule drugs that bind to deep, well-defined pockets, PPI interfaces often comprise broad, shallow binding surfaces. A natural strategy is to leverage known peptide–target interactions, as peptide ligands provide rich interface-level constraints. However, a major algorithmic challenge is that rigid atom-level conditioning on peptide structures can over-constrain the generative space and exclude valid small-molecule solutions. To address this challenge, we present PIFT (Peptide InterFace Transfer), a novel framework that transfers peptide–target interaction patterns to small molecules through joint sampling-time guidance of masked discrete diffusion and continuous flow matching. PIFT first maps peptide–target and small-molecule–target interfaces into a shared, target-conditioned interaction space, capturing transferable interface information across molecular modalities. The resulting peptide-derived reference then jointly steers building-block logits and 3D coordinates toward peptide-compatible molecules while preserving a strong adapted molecular prior. Extensive experiments across diverse PPI targets show that the learned representation captures cross-modal interaction compatibility, while peptide guidance improves interface recovery and achieves strong docking performance and favorable molecular properties.

attrs.research_question: 如何通过局部性控制的采样时引导，在保持调控DNA序列合理性的同时，同时优化活性、新颖性和合理性，以解决现有方法的奖励黑客问题。

attrs.abstract: Designing regulatory DNA sequences for targeted gene-expression control is an important challenge. Recent approaches frame this task as property-conditioned generation, where diffusion models trained on natural sequences are guided toward high predicted activity through reward-based fine-tuning or sampling-time guidance. We show that single-reward evaluation can obscure reward-hacking behavior. By decomposing evaluation into property, novelty, and plausibility, we identify an empirically underexplored region of the evaluation space in which all three objectives are satisfied, but no existing baseline succeeds. We postulate that this gap arises because prior methods treat guidance primarily as a matter of magnitude. In regulatory DNA, however, sequence grammar is spatially nonuniform: motif positions are sensitive to perturbation, while background regions allow more exploration. We therefore propose LOCOGEN by reformulating guidance as a problem of locality. LOCOGEN learns an invariant motif mask through sequence-level invariance learning to protect motif positions, while applying OOD damping only to background positions. It operates at sampling time on a frozen diffusion backbone, without retraining the backbone. Across HepG2, K562, and SK-N-SH, LOCOGEN reaches this previously underexplored region of the property–novelty–plausibility space. Code is available at https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/LocoGen.

attrs.research_question: 如何利用基于LLM的智能体自动操作磁光克尔显微镜，通过CNN感知与确定性安全层闭环控制磁天线的成像、分析与激励实验。
attrs.why_hard: 传统实验循环中每一步都需要实验人员判断，且现有图像处理方法需针对每次测量手动重新设计，无法可靠分离缺陷。
attrs.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topological spin textures that can be observed directly by magnetic microscopy and driven by fields and currents, which makes them a model system for fundamental physics and candidates for spintronic devices. Magneto-optical Kerr microscopy is a method to image them in real time; however, most experiments use an inefficient cycle of consecutive imaging, analysis and excitation in which every step requires the judgement of the experimentalist operating the setup. Here we present the Agentic AI Kerr Lab (AgentKerr), in which an agent based on a large language model operates this cycle automatically and efficiently on a Kerr microscope. Rather than relying on pattern detection by a language model, a convolutional neural network trained on Kerr images turns live images into skyrmion observables such as position, size and shape, on which the agent bases its decisions. The architecture lets agents operate the instruments safely, as every hardware action is checked deterministically against an action policy, independently of the agent that issues it. With no procedure given, the agent determines by itself how to create, tune and move skyrmions, and writes its own analyses. The approach can be transferred to other spin textures and points towards magnetic imaging experiments in which the researcher poses the question and the agent finds the way to realize the experiments that yield the answer.

attrs.research_question: 研究智能体在抗体设计任务中遵循指令的保真度及其影响因素，比较任务引导与黑盒设计模式下的性能。
attrs.why_hard: 现有基准独立评估蛋白设计性能或文本指令遵循，缺乏联合评估智能体在蛋白工程中既遵循指令又提升亲和力的能力。
attrs.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated agents driving protein design workflows, either through orchestration of specialized tools or direct manipulation of sequences. Yet the fidelity with which agents follow protein design instructions and the factors contributing to their effectiveness remain understudied. We examine agentic antibody design under two settings: when explicit molecular-editing instructions are provided and when agents receive only previously-scored sequences and are prompted to propose improvements. We call the first task-guided and the second black-box design. For the task-guided setting, we curate ten expert-validated affinity-improvement tasks and show that LLM judges closely reproduce programmatic evaluations of instruction following. We then study two augmentations: access to antibody-relevant tools and to previously scored design history. Tools improve instruction following (IF) and sequence space exploration while reducing optimization performance, whereas design history reduces IF but improves optimization performance at the expense of exploration. Finally, we combine task-guided and black-box design within an in silico optimization loop and show that our agentic optimizer performs comparably to an established Bayesian optimization baseline.

attrs.research_question: 提出HamFormer，一种基于Hamiltonian flow的SE(3)-Transformer架构，用于分子构象优化。
attrs.why_hard: 现有动力学解释方法主要关注单个注意力头，且很少考虑SE(3)-等变性。
attrs.abstract: The Transformer architecture plays a central role in modern deep learning, and its SE(3)-equivariant variants have been widely applied to molecular conformation modeling and optimization. Given its importance, many methods attempt to interpret and improve the Transformer through the lens of dynamics. However, they mainly focus on a single attention head rather than the full Transformer architecture and seldom consider SE(3)-equivariance in their proposed models. In this study, we propose an improved SE(3)-Transformer architecture, called HamFormer, which revisits the design of SE(3)-Transformer through the lens of Hamiltonian flow. In particular, we define a parametrized Hamiltonian flow in the phase space of position and velocity, corresponding to optimizing an energy functional that combines an optimal transport-based potential with a damped momentum. The Lie-Trotter splitting framework of the Hamiltonian flow leads to the proposed HamFormer architecture, whose feedforward computation achieves the optimization step of the proposed energy functional. Furthermore, we combine HamFormer with Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN), build a new model for molecular conformation optimization. Extensive experiments on molecular ground-state conformation prediction show that HamFormer provides a strong and physically interpretable surrogate for classic SE(3)-Transformer and generally outperforms state-of-the-art competitors.

attrs.title: From FAIR to AI-FAIR: Metadata-First Infrastructure for
attrs.label: From FAIR to AI-FAIR: Metadata-First Infrastructure for
attrs.research_question: 提出AI-FAIR元数据标准及代理评估工作流，以解决生态与生物多样性科学中数据基础设施碎片化及AI就绪性问题。
attrs.why_hard: 现有FAIR原则不足以指导AI就绪基础设施，数据碎片化、格式不一致且缺乏机器可操作性，导致AI工作流难以复用数据。
attrs.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their capabilities have advanced rapidly over the past few years, leading to widespread interest and adoption in the biological and ecological sciences. However, the data infrastructure and computational resources that provide the foundation for AI workflows in ecology and biodiversity science remain fragmented. Moreover, the flow of value remains largely unidirectional: data move from collectors, through repositories and aggregators into models, and finally to research products or management actions. The derived value, such as corrected taxonomies, annotations, quality flags, and insights, rarely returns to source communities. We propose an extension of the original FAIR principles to address the needs of AI-ready infrastructure: the AI-FAIR metadata criteria, which place AI-enabled science in the context of a bidirectional Question–Data–Model triangle. This framework is designed to facilitate large-scale content-based analysis across diverse collections and ensure that the scientists generating the data benefit from the AI-enabled advances built on their data. Alongside these criteria, we introduce an agentic evaluation workflow 1 that both rates existing datasets on the AI-FAIR and traditional FAIR criteria and provides actionable feedback where critical metadata is missing or incomplete. This modular dataset evaluation tool, paired with a domain-appropriate checklist, translates these principles into a reusable assessment of machine-learning readiness, AI-readiness for specified tasks, traceability, and ethical and CARE-aligned stewardship. Through this approach we aim to create a community-informed system to close the model data loop, so that AI also enriches data to further enable scientific discovery.

attrs.research_question: 提出Verso MAELLE，一种基于电子推动离散流匹配和Feynman-Kac引导的单步逆合成模型，以解决现有模型缺乏策略性引导和电子重排推理的问题。
attrs.why_hard: 现有单步逆合成模型的反应分布固定于训练数据，且通过从头生成或图编辑预测反应，忽略了控制化学转化的电子重排。
attrs.abstract: Expert chemists perform retrosynthetic analysis in a strategic manner, where each reaction in a route is employed with a specific purpose, combined with mechanistic reasoning represented as electron-pushing arrows to visualize how bonds are formed or broken via electron redistribution. Yet contemporary single-step retrosynthesis models exhibit neither of these properties: their learned reaction distribution is fixed to that of the training data, and reactions are predicted via de-novo generation of the precursors or molecular graph edits, omitting the electron redistribution that governs the chemical transformations. We introduce Verso MAELLE, the first electron-pushing-based single-step retrosynthetic model, representing disconnections as continuous-time Markov chains (CTMC) comprised of edits in the electron space, and is trainable using a discrete flow matching formulation. Being a generative model, Verso MAELLE is optionally steerable at inference time through the Feynman-Kac (FK) framework, using rewards that promote certain types of disconnections. We show that besides in-distribution learning, Verso MAELLE can be steered toward cyclization reactions which are scaffold-constructive but underrepresented in the training corpus, via a ring-breaking reward. As a proof of concept, we show how the electron-pushing reasoning, learned from patented data, combined with a domino incentivizing reward, could steer Verso MAELLE toward creative and strategic disconnections, demonstrated on the key domino sequence that was used to synthesize Punctaporonin U, a complex natural product of the sesquiterpene family.

attrs.abstract: Protein–protein interactions underpin nearly all biological processes. Yet, designing proteins with desired interactions remains challenging due to the structural complexity governing molecular recognition. This study views protein design as a search optimization problem over a combinatorial sequence space under expensive structural evaluation. Toward this goal, we introduce a novel tree-based search framework, ProteoCraft, that employs approximate structural gradients from diffusion-based structure predictors as effective proposal policies to specify where the search should explore. Complete no-gradient inference of folding models separately assigns values to the resulting sequences, determining what is good. ProteoCraft allocates this verification budget through a coarse-to-fine paradigm: multi-site edits first explore distinct sequence basins, then verified promising states undergo strict single-site refinement. Across fourteen de novo binder-design settings spanning eight target proteins, five immune-relevant TCR-facing targets, and four localized CDR redesign tasks, ProteoCraft improves design quality and high-confidence yield. These improvements persist under independent AF2-IG and Rosetta-based interface evaluation. Prospective experimental validation further yielded an 82.9% binding hit rate for PD-L1 miniproteins, with a best measured KD of 0.879 nM, and confirmed binding of designed IFNAR2 VHH. Our code is available at https://github.com/smiles724/ProteoCraft_v1.

attrs.abstract: Graph generation has shown tremendous effectiveness in modeling complex scientific tasks ranging from molecule generation to optimized circuit design. Most recent advancements have developed models that learn to denoise noisy graphs using either discrete diffusion or flow matching. However, discrete graph diffusion scales quadratically with the number of nodes, making it difficult to use such models on larger graphs. On the other hand, latent graph generation instead seeks to denoise noisy graph latents, which scale better to more nodes due to their lower dimension. However, in practice, latent graph generation models lag behind their discrete counterparts in performance. We study this problem, finding that it is caused by the unequal distribution of that different latent dimensions have on graph reconstruction. the impact. We observe that the vast majority of impact is contained in only a smaller number of latent dimensions. Since equal emphasis is placed on reconstructing the entire latent in the loss function, existing models are optimized to reconstruct information irrelevant to the downstream task. To tackle this problem, we propose Latent Importance Reweighting (LIR) which weights each latent dimensions via it’s importance to final graph reconstruction. Importance is calculated as the relative influence of a single latent unit on graph reconstruction, which is represented via the Jacobian of the decoder relative to the latent. Our method is model-agnostic and requires no additional model parameters or hyperparameters. Experiments show that LIR can boost performance and lead to faster training convergence when applied to two different autoencoders on various benchmark datasets.

attrs.abstract: Diffusion models have recently emerged as a powerful paradigm for generating 3D molecules. Despite showing remarkable promise, they learn atomic distributions implicitly from data, without explicitly encoding physicochemical rules into their generative dynamics. Consequently, generated samples can be statistically plausible yet chemically invalid. To address this problem, we propose Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constrained Diffusion (SensDiff), a framework that integrates symbolic rules into generative modeling, enabling the model to internalize scientific priors during training. Central to SensDiff is the observation that the diffusion trajectory of 3D molecule generation exhibits a coarse-to-fine evolution: valid molecules arise by first mitigating macroscopic geometric conflicts and then refining structures toward microscopic chemical consistency through iterative denoising. Accordingly, SensDiff mirrors this dynamic by sequentially enforcing constraints with adaptive weighting during training, progressively steering generation toward valid molecular geometries. Moreover, SensDiff translates domain knowledge into interpretable generative controls, grounding opaque neural denoising in scientific principles. Experiments on molecular benchmarks and real-world constrained generation tasks confirm that SensDiff consistently improves chemical validity while adhering to physicochemical rules and user-specified targets. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/NeurIPS2026_SensDiff.

attrs.abstract: Long-term particle physics experiments face critical operational challenges: monitoring non-stationary machine data streams and preserving tacit expert knowledge. We present the “Helmholtz Co-Pilot,” a hybrid Multi-Agent System (MAS) acting as an autonomous experiment steward. The system can be triggered interactively by human operators or autonomously by an asynchronous causal diagnostics engine that runs independently of the MAS reasoning core. Continuously monitoring live hardware streams such as data acquisition and slow control, this engine performs dynamic causal discovery to trace cascading alarms back to their root causes and applies adaptive model selection to keep forecasts reliable across shifting machine states; upon detecting an anomaly, it hands a structured diagnostic report to the MAS. The reasoning layer itself relies on a high-throughput C++ core and a Python edge architecture orchestrating a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of specialized ReAct workers. It integrates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) backbone for institutional memory and leverages conformal prediction to bound its evidence-based recommendations with mathematical coverage guarantees. This extended abstract outlines the architecture, the integration of software-enforced Human-in-the-Loop (HitL) guardrails, and ongoing shadow-testing within the KATRIN experiment.

attrs.research_question: 在TDC ADMET的22个数据集上，哪种校准不确定性量化方法表现最佳，且该基准能解决什么比较问题？
attrs.why_hard: ADMET数据集小且异质，不同化学划分、模型初始化及调优数据会改变点预测器与UQ方法间的观测差异。
attrs.abstract: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) models often rely on small, heterogeneous datasets, yet their predictions may determine which compounds proceed to experimental testing. Useful evaluations must therefore assess both predictive performance and the quality of reported probabilities or intervals. We ask which common uncertainty-quantification methods perform best on the 22 Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) ADMET datasets and what this benchmark can resolve. We compare eleven calibrated pipelines using nested five-fold cross-validation across ten chemical partitions and five model seeds. Ensemble Monte Carlo (MC) dropout has the best average rank for TDC performance, Brier score, and 90% interval score. For TDC performance, however, it is not separated from the other ensemble pipelines; for Brier and interval score, LightGBM is also not ruled out as best. LightGBM wins more individual datasets than any other method for TDC performance and Brier score, but performs poorly on several endpoints. Smaller evaluations can identify a different leader and often fail to recover the broader comparison. These results make LightGBM and an ensemble neural model complementary baselines. Comparative claims should be checked across multiple chemical partitions using statistical analyses matched to the question being asked.

problems_solved: Existing diffusion-based 3D molecule generation methods suffer from unsatisfactory performances on large molecules.
Generated molecules lack enough diversity due to limited exploration in intermediate steps of Langevin dynamics.

attrs.why_it_works: Explicitly modeling covalent and van der Waals forces captures local constraints, while distributional conditioning prevents trajectory concentration and enhances diversity.

problems_solved: 解决连续归一化流（CNF）基于模拟的最大似然训练困难
提供无需模拟ODE的无模拟训练目标

attrs.mechanism: 通过回归ODE的漂移场（drift field）来训练CNF，利用条件概率路径构建稳定的回归目标，避免了对源分布密度的评估。
attrs.why_it_works: 回归目标比模拟更稳定，且不需要源分布为高斯或评估其密度，从而提高了训练效率和泛化能力。
applicable_to: 条件与无条件生成任务
limitations: 标准CFM未显式利用最优传输结构，可能导致流路径不够直，推理效率低于OT-CFM

problems_solved: 解决引导模型在分布外（OOD）区域泛化能力差的问题

提高条件扩散模型在缺乏标签数据区域生成高价值新分子/蛋白的可靠性

applicable_to: 材料科学中的新物质生成
蛋白质序列优化与设计
limitations: 需要额外的无标签上下文数据用于训练正则化器

attrs.name: Learned Equivariance via Rotation Augmentation
attrs.label: Learned Equivariance via Rotation Augmentation
problems_solved: Equivariant GNNs are complex, difficult to train, and scale poorly.
Explicit equivariance is assumed essential but may not be required for high-quality 3D molecules.
Need to evaluate if non-equivariant CNNs can match equivariant models via data augmentation.
attrs.mechanism: Trains non-equivariant 3D CNNs with random rotation and translation augmentations to learn approximate equivariance, and derives a loss decomposition to separate prediction error from equivariance error.
attrs.why_it_works: Data augmentation encourages learned equivariance without architectural constraints, allowing flexible architectures like CNNs to match or outperform equivariant GNNs in specific tasks.
limitations: Smaller models diverge and lose generative equivariance in generative tasks.
Latent embeddings of rotated molecules differ significantly, suggesting redundant parallel representations.
Higher parameter demands compared to equivariant GNNs.

attrs.name: Pretrained Joint Predictions for Scalable Batch Bayesian Opt
attrs.label: Pretrained Joint Predictions for Scalable Batch Bayesian Opt
problems_solved: 解决高斯过程在大规模数据集上立方级缩放导致的计算瓶颈
解决深度集成方法在批量贝叶斯优化中采样效率低且参数冗余的问题
实现结合亲和力联合预测分布的快速采样以支持并行获取函数
attrs.mechanism: 基于认知神经网络（ENN）框架，利用预训练的先验网络处理来自大型结构感知模型的潜在表示，通过边缘化潜在索引而非参数来高效生成联合预测分布。
attrs.why_it_works: 预训练先验网络改善了联合对数损失，使得ENN能够以参数高效的方式建模联合预测分布，从而加速批量贝叶斯优化的收敛。
applicable_to: 小分子药物发现中的结合亲和力优化
大规模分子库的批量筛选
基于基础模型表示的代理模型构建
limitations: qPO获取函数的近似需要大量独立同分布样本路径才能收敛
qPO的计算复杂度随候选池大小线性增加

attrs.name: Epistemic Neural Network (ENN)
attrs.mechanism: 通过边缘化潜在分布p_Z(z)而非参数θ来构建联合预测分布
attrs.formula: p ( y _ { 1 : N } | x _ { 1 : N } ) = \int _ { z } \delta \left( [ f _ { \theta } ( x _ { i } , z ) ] _ { 1 : N } = y _ { 1 : N } \right) p _ { Z } ( z ) \mathr
attrs.inputs: 分子潜在表示 x, 潜在索引 z
attrs.label: Epistemic Neural Network (ENN)

attrs.name: Joint Sampling Module
attrs.mechanism: 从联合预测密度中快速采样以近似并行获取函数
attrs.inputs: ENN模型, 候选分子集合
attrs.label: Joint Sampling Module

attrs.name: Parallel Acquisition Function
attrs.mechanism: 利用联合样本计算qPO或EMAX以平衡批次内设计的对冲与利用
attrs.formula: \mathbb { E } _ { p ( y _ { 1 : N } ) } \left[ \operatorname* { m a x } ( \hat { y } _ { 1 : N } ) \leq \operatorname* { m a x } ( \hat { y } _ { 1 : B } ) \rig
attrs.inputs: 联合样本路径, 候选池
attrs.label: Parallel Acquisition Function

attrs.name: Custom GP Implementation
attrs.mechanism: 直接处理RDKit指纹对象并计算Tanimoto相似度矩阵
attrs.formula: k(x, x') = a^2 k_Tanimoto(x, x') + sigma_n^2 delta(x, x')

attrs.name: Tanimoto Kernel
attrs.mechanism: 计算两个分子指纹向量之间的Tanimoto相似度
attrs.formula: k_Tanimoto(x, x') = sum_i min(x_i, x'_i) / sum_i max(x_i, x'_i)
attrs.label: Tanimoto Kernel

problems_solved: 解决生成模型倾向于采样高概率模式而忽略低概率但高价值区域的问题
解决生成模型难以直接采样到进化上不可达但功能最优区域的问题
解决生成模型分布与用户指定属性分布不一致的问题
attrs.mechanism: 通过参数更新对齐（如SFT、RL）或参数固定引导（如条件生成、贝叶斯引导、采样控制）策略，将生成分布从p(x)引导至p(x|y)。
attrs.why_it_works: 通过调整模型参数或引导生成过程，使模型能够访问低概率但功能最优的蛋白质空间区域，从而生成具有特定属性的蛋白质。
limitations: SFT无法区分数据质量，可能导致灾难性遗忘
仅增加模型规模不保证拟合预测单调改进
训练数据中的系统发育表示不均和标注错误可能扭曲学习景观

problems_solved: 解决化学空间巨大导致的高保真模拟成本高昂问题
克服现有方法依赖连续潜在空间导致的架构纠缠和可扩展性挑战
实现样本高效的新分子多目标设计，扩展Pareto前沿
attrs.mechanism: 采用“先生成后优化”的两阶段框架：第一阶段利用生成模型构建大规模候选池，第二阶段使用qPMHI采集函数通过蒙特卡洛采样估计最大超体积改进概率，以选择最优批次。
attrs.why_it_works: qPMHI具有可加性分解结构，允许通过简单的概率排序进行精确且可扩展的批次选择，无需组合优化，且解耦了生成模型与代理模型。
limitations: 依赖生成模型产生足够多样且合理的候选池
需要足够的标记数据训练概率代理模型

attrs.label: Generative Proposal Module

attrs.name: qPMHI Acquisition Function

problems_solved: Detects verbatim retrieval of memorized target values in LLMs.
Analyzes conflicts between pre-trained knowledge and in-context information.
Evaluates genuine in-context regression capabilities under controlled information access.
attrs.mechanism: Progressively removes contextual information (property names, chemical terminology) and transforms target values/SMILES across six levels to isolate memorization from generalization.

limitations: Requires manual definition of blinding levels and transformations.
Limited to datasets where SMILES and target values can be transformed.

attrs.name: Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian from Effective Field Theory
attrs.label: Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian from Effective Field Theory
problems_solved: KS bandwidths overestimate ARPES measurements by 20-35% in alkali metals
Lack of physical justification for KS eigenvalues as quasiparticle energies
Conventional pseudopotentials fail to capture dynamical core excitations
attrs.mechanism: Constructs an EFT of the inhomogeneous electron gas by integrating out core electrons via dual-fermion transformation and applying Galilean invariance to derive a frozen-core renormalization factor.
attrs.why_it_works: Scale separation between core and valence energies allows controlled expansion, and approximate Galilean invariance ensures the tree-level propagator retains KS form with a dynamical correction.
applicable_to: Systems with significant core-valence scale separation
limitations: Requires scale separation between core excitation energies and valence Fermi energy
Relies on approximate Galilean invariance of the uniform electron gas

attrs.name: Dual-Fermion Core Integration
attrs.mechanism: Integrates out core Grassmann fields to produce valence effective action
attrs.label: Dual-Fermion Core Integration

attrs.name: Frozen-Core Renormalization
attrs.mechanism: Calculates closed-form renormalization factor from core form factors
attrs.inputs: Core form factors, core excitation energies, Bloch coefficients
attrs.label: Frozen-Core Renormalization

attrs.name: Quasiparticle Propagator Derivation
attrs.mechanism: Derives tree-level quasiparticle propagator using Galilean invariance
attrs.inputs: Valence effective action, KS eigenvalues, Fermi energy
attrs.label: Quasiparticle Propagator Derivation

attrs.name: Quasiparticle Energy Correction
attrs.mechanism: Applies frozen-core factor to KS eigenvalues to predict quasiparticle energies
attrs.inputs: KS eigenvalues, Fermi energy, frozen-core renormalization factor
attrs.label: Quasiparticle Energy Correction

problems_solved: 评估通用机器学习原子势在高温MOF动力学中的鲁棒性
量化uMLIPs在极端温度下的能量、力和应力误差
揭示静态验证损失与长时程模拟生成误差之间的差异
attrs.mechanism: 构建高温AIMD轨迹数据集，使用ORB-v3、MACE和fairchem等uMLIPs进行分子动力学模拟，并与DFT参考值对比计算误差。
attrs.why_it_works: 通过覆盖平衡、热畸变和早期分解阶段的高温轨迹，系统性地测试模型在域外高能量区域的预测能力。
applicable_to: 高温金属有机框架动力学模拟
机器学习原子势的基准测试
材料高温分解机制研究
limitations: 所有模型在高温条件下均表现出显著误差
uMLIPs的生成误差远超静态验证捕获的模型损失

limitations: The random tape has no obvious metric, limiting navigation.
Native-coordinate volume has no automatic chemical meaning.

problems_solved: 解决AI设计抗体候选数量远超实验验证能力的问题
在有限实验预算下优先筛选出真正结合抗原的候选抗体
平衡假阳性（浪费实验资源）与假阴性（丢弃真结合体）的风险
attrs.mechanism: 利用结构预测模型输出的置信度指标（如ipTM, pLDDT）及新提出的RIC和NAC指标，对AI生成的抗体-抗原复合物进行打分和排序，以决定哪些候选进入实验验证。
attrs.why_it_works: 结构预测输出包含关于结合能力的部分信号；非CDR区域的抗体置信度（NAC）提供了超越界面证据的额外过滤信号，特别是在同一抗原内的候选排序中更有效。
applicable_to: AI设计抗体的后生成筛选
基于结构预测的抗体-抗原复合物优先级排序
limitations: 性能最终受限于结构预测模型本身能区分的信号上限
预测结构包含的结合相关信号是不完整的

problems_solved: 评估LLM嵌入科学代理框架后安全性是否保持
量化代理框架对有害请求合规率的影响
揭示自适应攻击在代理环境下的成功率变化
attrs.mechanism: 固定基础LLM，对比其单独运行与嵌入五个科学代理框架（CACTUS, ChemToolAgent等）在直接提示、角色扮演、过去时态及PAIR自适应攻击下的有害化学请求响应，计算攻击成功率差异（ΔASR）。
attrs.why_it_works: 通过控制变量（固定基础模型）并引入多种提示策略，能够隔离代理框架本身对模型安全行为的影响，区分基础模型固有安全与系统级安全退化。
applicable_to: LLM代理框架的鲁棒性评估
有害化学请求的防御机制研究
limitations: PAIR实验因计算成本高未重复运行
仅评估了五个特定的科学代理框架
仅针对化学领域的有害请求
